sanskrit: sādhubhir garhitaṃ karma caṇḍālasya vidhīyate kasmād gorajasā dhvastam apāṃ kuṇḍe niṣiñcasi
english: "The work assigned to a Caṇḍāla is condemned by the virtuous. Why do you pour into a vessel of water that which has been defiled by the dust raised by cattle?"

sanskrit: caṇḍāla uvāca brāhmaṇasya gavāṃ rājan hriyatīnāṃ rajaḥ purā somam uddhvaṃsayām āsa taṃ somaṃ ye 'piban dvijāḥ
english: The Caṇḍāla said: O king, in a former age the dust raised by a Brahmin's cattle, as they were being driven off, defiled the Soma; and the twice-born who then drank that Soma—

sanskrit: dīkṣitaś ca sa rājāpi kṣipraṃ narakam āviśat saha tair yājakaiḥ sarvair brahmasvam upajīvya tat
english: And that consecrated king too, together with all his officiating priests, swiftly entered hell, for they had lived off that property belonging to a Brahmin.

sanskrit: ye 'pi tatrāpiban kṣīraṃ ghṛtaṃ dadhi ca mānavāḥ brāhmaṇāḥ saharājanyāḥ sarve narakam āviśan
english: And those men who there drank the milk, the clarified butter, and the curds—Brahmins together with the Kṣatriyas—all of them entered hell.

sanskrit: jaghnus tāḥ payasā putrāṃs tathā pautrān vidhunvatīḥ paśūn avekṣamāṇāś ca sādhuvṛttena daṃpatī
english: By that milk the husband and wife, watching over their cattle in righteous conduct, struck down their own sons and grandsons as the cows tossed and shook themselves.

sanskrit: ahaṃ tatrāvasaṃ rājan brahmacārī jitendriyaḥ tāsāṃ me rajasā dhvastaṃ bhaikṣam āsīn narādhipa
english: I dwelt there, O king, a celibate student with my senses subdued; and the alms I had gathered, O lord of men, were defiled by the dust of those cows.

sanskrit: caṇḍālo 'haṃ tato rājan bhuktvā tad abhavaṃ mṛtaḥ brahmasvahārī ca nṛpaḥ so 'pratiṣṭhāṃ gatiṃ yayau
english: Having eaten that, O king, I became a Caṇḍāla when I died; and that king who stole a Brahmin's property came to a state without any foundation.

sanskrit: tasmād dharen na viprasvaṃ kadā cid api kiṃ cana brahmasvarajasā dhvastaṃ bhuktvā māṃ paśya yādṛśam
english: Therefore let no one ever take anything whatever of a Brahmin's wealth. Look upon me—what I have become—for having eaten what was defiled by the dust of a Brahmin's property.

sanskrit: tasmāt somo 'py avikreyaḥ puruṣeṇa vipaścitā vikrayaṃ hīha somasya garhayanti manīṣiṇaḥ
english: Therefore even the Soma must not be sold by a discerning man, for the wise here condemn the sale of Soma.

sanskrit: ye cainaṃ krīṇate rājan ye ca vikrīṇate janāḥ te tu vaivasvataṃ prāpya rauravaṃ yānti sarvaśaḥ
english: Those people who buy it, O king, and those who sell it, all alike, on reaching the abode of the son of Vivasvat, go to the hell Raurava.

sanskrit: somaṃ tu rajasā dhvastaṃ vikrīyād buddhipūrvakam śrotriyo vārdhuṣī bhūtvā cirarātrāya naśyati narakaṃ triṃśataṃ prāpya śvaviṣṭhām upajīvati
english: But should a learned reciter of the Veda knowingly sell Soma that has been defiled by dust, becoming a usurer he is ruined for a long night of time; reaching the thirty hells, he subsists upon the dung of dogs.

sanskrit: śvacaryām atimānaṃ ca sakhidāreṣu viplavam tulayādhārayad dharmo hy atimāno 'tiricyate
english: The life of a dog, excessive pride, and transgression against the wives of friends—Dharma weighed these in the balance, and excessive pride proved the heaviest of all.

sanskrit: śvānaṃ vai pāpinaṃ paśya vivarṇaṃ hariṇaṃ kṛśam atimānena bhūtānām imāṃ gatim upāgatam
english: Look upon this sinful dog, discolored, tawny, and lean, who through excessive pride toward living beings has come to this condition.

sanskrit: ahaṃ vai vipule jātaḥ kule dhanasamanvite anyasmiñ janmani vibho jñānavijñānapāragaḥ
english: In another birth, O mighty one, I was born into a great family endowed with wealth, having mastered both knowledge and discernment.

sanskrit: abhavaṃ tatra jānāno hy etān doṣān madāt tadā saṃrabdha eva bhūtānāṃ pṛṣṭhamāṃsāny abhakṣayam
english: Although I knew these faults, I yet acted out of arrogance then; in my fury I devoured the flesh from the backs of living creatures.

sanskrit: so 'haṃ tena ca vṛttena bhojanena ca tena vai imām avasthāṃ saṃprāptaḥ paśya kālasya paryayam
english: And so, by that conduct and by that eating, I have come to this state. Behold the turning of time!

sanskrit: ādīptam iva cailāntaṃ bhramarair iva cārditam dhāvamānaṃ susaṃrabdhaṃ paśya māṃ rajasānvitam
english: Behold me, as if my garment's hem were ablaze, as if tormented by bees, running about in a frenzy, covered with dust.

sanskrit: svādhyāyais tu mahat pāpaṃ taranti gṛhamedhinaḥ dānaiḥ pṛthagvidhaiś cāpi yathā prāhur manīṣiṇaḥ
english: By recitation of the sacred texts householders cross over great sin, and likewise by gifts of many kinds, even as the wise have declared.

sanskrit: tathā pāpakṛtaṃ vipram āśramasthaṃ mahīpate sarvasaṅgavinirmuktaṃ chandāṃsy uttārayanty uta
english: Even so, O lord of the earth, when a Brahmin who has done evil abides in his hermitage, freed from all attachments, the sacred meters carry him across.

sanskrit: ahaṃ tu pāpayonyāṃ vai prasūtaḥ kṣatriyarṣabha niścayaṃ nādhigacchāmi kathaṃ mucyeyam ity uta
english: But I, O bull among Kṣatriyas, born in a sinful womb, can reach no certainty as to how I might be set free.

sanskrit: jātismaratvaṃ tu mama kena cit pūrvakarmaṇā śubhena yena mokṣaṃ vai prāptum icchāmy ahaṃ nṛpa
english: This memory of my former births is mine by reason of some auspicious deed in the past—by that, O king, I desire to attain release.

sanskrit: tvam imaṃ me prapannāya saṃśayaṃ brūhi pṛcchate caṇḍālatvāt katham ahaṃ mucyeyam iti sattama
english: Tell me, who have come to you and ask, the resolution of this doubt, O best of men: how may I be freed from this state of being a Caṇḍāla?

sanskrit: rājanya uvāca caṇḍāla pratijānīhi yena mokṣam avāpsyasi brāhmaṇārthe tyajan prāṇān gatim iṣṭām avāpsyasi
english: The Kṣatriya said: Caṇḍāla, resolve upon that by which you shall win release. Laying down your life for the sake of a Brahmin, you shall attain the longed-for goal.

sanskrit: dattvā śarīraṃ kravyādbhyo raṇāgnau dvijahetukam hutvā prāṇān pramokṣas te nānyathā mokṣam arhasi
english: Giving up your body to the flesh-eaters in the fire of battle for the sake of the twice-born, offering up your breath as oblation—that is your release; in no other way can you merit it.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca ity uktaḥ sa tadā rājan brahmasvārthe paraṃtapa hutvā raṇamukhe prāṇān gatim iṣṭām avāpa ha
english: Bhīṣma said: Thus addressed, O king, scorcher of foes, he then offered up his life in the forefront of battle for the sake of a Brahmin's property, and won the goal he had longed for.

sanskrit: tasmād rakṣyaṃ tvayā putra brahmasvaṃ bharatarṣabha yadīcchasi mahābāho śāśvatīṃ gatim uttamām
english: Therefore the property of Brahmins must be guarded by you, my son, O bull of the Bhāratas, if you desire, O mighty-armed one, the eternal and supreme goal.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca eko lokaḥ sukṛtināṃ sarve tv āho pitāmaha uta tatrāpi nānātvaṃ tan me brūhi pitāmaha
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Is there but one world for all the doers of good deeds, O grandsire, or is there even there a diversity of worlds? Tell me this, O grandsire.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca karmabhiḥ pārtha nānātvaṃ lokānāṃ yānti mānavāḥ puṇyān puṇyakṛto yānti pāpān pāpakṛto janāḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: By their deeds, O Pārtha, men attain a diversity of worlds: the doers of merit go to meritorious worlds, and those who do evil go to evil ones.

sanskrit: atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam gautamasya munes tāta saṃvādaṃ vāsavasya ca
english: On this point too, my son, they recount this ancient tale: the dialogue between the sage Gautama and Vāsava.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇo gautamaḥ kaś cin mṛdur dānto jitendriyaḥ mahāvane hastiśiśuṃ paridyūnam amātṛkam
english: A certain Brahmin named Gautama—gentle, self-restrained, his senses subdued—found in the great forest an elephant calf, wasted away and motherless.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā jīvayām āsa sānukrośo dhṛtavrataḥ sa tu dīrgheṇa kālena babhūvātibalo mahān
english: Seeing it, that man of firm vows, full of compassion, nursed it back to life; and in the course of a long time it became great and exceedingly strong.

sanskrit: taṃ prabhinnaṃ mahānāgaṃ prasrutaṃ sarvato madam dhṛtarāṣṭrasya rūpeṇa śakro jagrāha hastinam
english: That mighty elephant, its temples split with rut, streaming ichor on every side—Śakra, in the form of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, seized.

sanskrit: hriyamāṇaṃ tu taṃ dṛṣṭvā gautamaḥ saṃśitavrataḥ abhyabhāṣata rājānaṃ dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ mahātapāḥ
english: Seeing the elephant being carried off, Gautama of stern vows and great austerity addressed the king Dhṛtarāṣṭra:

sanskrit: mā me hārṣīr hastinaṃ putram enaṃ; duḥkhāt puṣṭaṃ dhṛtarāṣṭrākṛtajña mitraṃ satāṃ saptapadaṃ vadanti; mitradroho naiva rājan spṛśet tvām
english: "Do not steal from me this elephant, my own son, whom I reared up out of hardship, O ungrateful Dhṛtarāṣṭra! The good say that friendship is sealed in seven steps walked together; let not the betrayal of a friend, O king, ever touch you."

sanskrit: idhmodakapradātāraṃ śūnyapālakam āśrame vinītam ācāryakule suyuktaṃ gurukarmaṇi
english: "He brings me kindling and water, and guards the hermitage when it is empty; disciplined in the teacher's household, well-engaged in his master's service—"

sanskrit: śiṣṭaṃ dāntaṃ kṛtajñaṃ ca priyaṃ ca satataṃ mama na me vikrośato rājan hartum arhasi kuñjaram
english: "—well-trained, tame, grateful, and ever dear to me. While I cry out in protest, O king, you ought not to carry off my elephant."

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca gavāṃ sahasraṃ bhavate dadāmi; dāsīśataṃ niṣkaśatāni pañca anyac ca vittaṃ vividhaṃ maharṣe; kiṃ brāhmaṇasyeha gajena kṛtyam
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: "I will give to you a thousand cows, a hundred handmaidens, five hundred gold coins, and other wealth of many kinds, great sage. What use here has a Brahmin for an elephant?"

sanskrit: gautama uvāca tvām eva gāvo 'bhi bhavantu rājan; dāsyaḥ saniṣkā vividhaṃ ca ratnam anyac ca vittaṃ vividhaṃ narendra; kiṃ brāhmaṇasyeha dhanena kṛtyam
english: Gautama said: "Let the cows belong to you alone, O king, the handmaidens together with the gold, and gems of many kinds, and other wealth besides, O lord of men. What use here has a Brahmin for riches?"

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca brāhmaṇānāṃ hastibhir nāsti kṛtyaṃ; rājanyānāṃ nāgakulāni vipra svaṃ vāhanaṃ nayato nāsty adharmo; nāgaśreṣṭhād gautamāsmān nivarta
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: "Brahmins have no use for elephants; herds of elephants belong to Kṣatriyas, O Brahmin. There is no unrighteousness in one who takes away his own mount. Turn aside, Gautama, from this best of elephants."

sanskrit: gautama uvāca yatra preto nandati puṇyakarmā; yatra pretaḥ śocati pāpakarmā vaivasvatasya sadane mahātmanas; tatra tvāhaṃ hastinaṃ yātayiṣye
english: Gautama said: "There, in the abode of the great-souled son of Vivasvat, where the departed doer of good deeds rejoices and the departed doer of evil deeds grieves—there will I haul you before judgment over this elephant."

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca ye niṣkriyā nāstikāḥ śraddadhānāḥ; pāpātmāna indriyārthe niviṣṭāḥ yamasya te yātanāṃ prāpnuvanti; paraṃ gantā dhṛtarāṣṭro na tatra
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: "Those who shun all rites, the unbelievers, and those of false faith, sinful souls sunk in the objects of sense—they meet the torment of Yama; but Dhṛtarāṣṭra, journeying onward, will not go there."

sanskrit: gautama uvāca vaivasvatī saṃyamanī janānāṃ; yatrānṛtaṃ nocyate yatra satyam yatrābalā balinaṃ yātayanti; tatra tvāhaṃ hastinaṃ yātayiṣye
english: Gautama said: "In the city of restraint belonging to the son of Vivasvat, where no falsehood is spoken but only truth, where the weak haul the strong before judgment—there will I haul you over this elephant."

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca jyeṣṭhāṃ svasāraṃ pitaraṃ mātaraṃ ca; guruṃ yathā mānayantaś caranti tathāvidhānām eṣa loko maharṣe; paraṃ gantā dhṛtarāṣṭro na tatra
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: "Those who go through life honoring an elder sister, a father, a mother, and a teacher as is fitting—to such people belongs this world, great sage; but Dhṛtarāṣṭra, journeying onward, will not go there."

sanskrit: gautama uvāca mandākinī vaiśravaṇasya rājño; mahābhogā bhogijanapraveśyā gandharvayakṣair apsarobhiś ca juṣṭā; tatra tvāhaṃ hastinaṃ yātayiṣye
english: Gautama said: "The Mandākinī of King Vaiśravaṇa, abounding in delights, open only to those who have earned their enjoyments, frequented by Gandharvas, Yakṣas, and Apsarases—there will I haul you over this elephant."

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca atithivratāḥ suvratā ye janā vai; pratiśrayaṃ dadati brāhmaṇebhyaḥ śiṣṭāśinaḥ saṃvibhajyāśritāṃś ca; mandākinīṃ te 'pi vibhūṣayanti
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: "Those people, firm in vows and devoted to guests, who give shelter to Brahmins, who eat only what is left after sharing, and who provide for their dependents—they too adorn the Mandākinī."

sanskrit: gautama uvāca meror agre yad vanaṃ bhāti ramyaṃ; supuṣpitaṃ kiṃnaragītajuṣṭam sudarśanā yatra jambūr viśālā; tatra tvāhaṃ hastinaṃ yātayiṣye
english: Gautama said: "That lovely forest which shines upon the summit of Meru, richly blossoming, filled with the songs of the Kiṃnaras, where stands the great and fair-to-see Jambū tree—there will I haul you over this elephant."

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca ye brāhmaṇā mṛdavaḥ satyaśīlā; bahuśrutāḥ sarvabhūtābhirāmāḥ ye 'dhīyante setihāsaṃ purāṇaṃ; madhvāhutyā juhvati ca dvijebhyaḥ
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: "Those Brahmins who are gentle, truthful in nature, deeply learned, delighting all beings, who study the Veda together with the Itihāsa and Purāṇa, and who make oblations of honey to the twice-born—"

sanskrit: tathāvidhānām eṣa loko maharṣe; paraṃ gantā dhṛtarāṣṭro na tatra yad vidyate viditaṃ sthānam asti; tad brūhi tvaṃ tvarito hy eṣa yāmi
english: "—to such men belongs this world, great sage; but Dhṛtarāṣṭra, journeying onward, will not go there. If there is some other known and certain place, name it—for I am in haste, and here I go."

sanskrit: gautama uvāca supuṣpitaṃ kiṃnararājajuṣṭaṃ; priyaṃ vanaṃ nandanaṃ nāradasya gandharvāṇām apsarasāṃ ca sadma; tatra tvāhaṃ hastinaṃ yātayiṣye
english: Gautama said: "The richly blossoming, beloved grove of Nārada, frequented by the king of the Kiṃnaras, the dwelling of the Gandharvas and the Apsarases—there will I haul you over this elephant."

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca ye nṛttagītakuśalā janāḥ sadā; hy ayācamānāḥ sahitāś caranti tathāvidhānām eṣa loko maharṣe; paraṃ gantā dhṛtarāṣṭro na tatra
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: "Those people who are ever skilled in dance and song, who go about in fellowship, never begging—to such belongs this world, great sage; but Dhṛtarāṣṭra, journeying onward, will not go there."

sanskrit: gautama uvāca yatrottarāḥ kuravo bhānti ramyā; devaiḥ sārdhaṃ modamānā narendra yatrāgniyaunāś ca vasanti viprā; hy ayonayaḥ parvatayonayaś ca
english: Gautama said: "Where the lovely Northern Kurus shine, rejoicing together with the gods, O lord of men, where dwell those Brahmins born of fire, those born of no womb, and those born of the mountains—"

sanskrit: yatra śakro varṣati sarvakāmān; yatra striyaḥ kāmacārāś caranti yatra cerṣyā nāsti nārīnarāṇāṃ; tatra tvāhaṃ hastinaṃ yātayiṣye
english: "—where Śakra rains down all that is desired, where women move at the pleasure of their own will, and where there is no jealousy between women and men—there will I haul you over this elephant."

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca ye sarvabhūteṣu nivṛttakāmā; amāṃsādā nyastadaṇḍāś caranti na hiṃsanti sthāvaraṃ jaṅgamaṃ ca; bhūtānāṃ ye sarvabhūtātmabhūtāḥ
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: "Those who go through life with their desires turned away from all beings, who eat no flesh and have laid down the rod, who harm neither the moving nor the unmoving, who have become one in self with all creatures—"

sanskrit: nirāśiṣo nirmamā vītarāgā; lābhālābhe tulyanindāpraśaṃsāḥ tathāvidhānām eṣa loko maharṣe; paraṃ gantā dhṛtarāṣṭro na tatra
english: "—free of longing, free of the sense of mine, devoid of passion, the same in gain and loss, in blame and in praise—to such men belongs this world, great sage; but Dhṛtarāṣṭra, journeying onward, will not go there."

sanskrit: gautama uvāca tataḥ paraṃ bhānti lokāḥ sanātanāḥ; supuṇyagandhā nirmalā vītaśokāḥ somasya rājñaḥ sadane mahātmanas; tatra tvāhaṃ hastinaṃ yātayiṣye
english: Gautama said: "Beyond that shine the eternal worlds, fragrant with holiness, stainless, free of sorrow, in the abode of the great-souled King Soma—there will I haul you over this elephant."

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca ye dānaśīlā na pratigṛhṇate sadā; na cāpy arthān ādadate parebhyaḥ yeṣām adeyam arhate nāsti kiṃ cit; sarvātithyāḥ suprasādā janāś ca
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: "Those of generous nature who never accept gifts, and who take no wealth from others, for whom nothing is too good to give to a worthy man, who are hospitable to all and serene of heart—"

sanskrit: ye kṣantāro nābhijalpanti cānyāñ; śaktā bhūtvā satataṃ puṇyaśīlāḥ tathāvidhānām eṣa loko maharṣe; paraṃ gantā dhṛtarāṣṭro na tatra
english: "—who are forbearing and, though able to retaliate, speak no harsh word against others, ever holy in conduct—to such men belongs this world, great sage; but Dhṛtarāṣṭra, journeying onward, will not go there."

sanskrit: gautama uvāca tataḥ paraṃ bhānti lokāḥ sanātanā; virajaso vitamaskā viśokāḥ ādityasya sumahāntaḥ suvṛttās; tatra tvāhaṃ hastinaṃ yātayiṣye
english: Gautama said: "Beyond that shine the eternal worlds, free of dust, free of darkness, free of sorrow, the vast and excellent worlds of Āditya—there will I haul you over this elephant."

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca svādhyāyaśīlā guruśuśrūṣaṇe ratās; tapasvinaḥ suvratāḥ satyasaṃdhāḥ ācāryāṇām apratikūlabhāṣiṇo; nityotthitā gurukarmasv acodyāḥ
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: "Those devoted to the study of the Veda, delighting in service to their elders, ascetics of firm vows, true to their word, who never speak against their teachers, ever alert and needing no prompting in their masters' tasks—"

sanskrit: tathāvidhānām eṣa loko maharṣe; viśuddhānāṃ bhāvitavāṅmatīnām satye sthitānāṃ vedavidāṃ mahātmanāṃ; paraṃ gantā dhṛtarāṣṭro na tatra
english: "—to such men belongs this world, great sage—to the pure, whose speech and mind are well-refined, who stand firm in truth, knowers of the Veda, great of soul; but Dhṛtarāṣṭra, journeying onward, will not go there."

sanskrit: gautama uvāca tataḥ pare bhānti lokāḥ sanātanāḥ; supuṇyagandhā virajā viśokāḥ varuṇasya rājñaḥ sadane mahātmanas; tatra tvāhaṃ hastinaṃ yātayiṣye
english: Gautama said: "Beyond that shine the eternal worlds, fragrant with holiness, free of dust, free of sorrow, in the abode of the great-souled King Varuṇa—there will I haul you over this elephant."

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca cāturmāsyair ye yajante janāḥ sadā; tatheṣṭīnāṃ daśaśataṃ prāpnuvanti ye cāgnihotraṃ juhvati śraddadhānā; yathānyāyaṃ trīṇi varṣāṇi viprāḥ
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: "Those people who ever sacrifice with the four-monthly rites, and so win the fruit of a thousand sacrificial offerings, and those Brahmins who, full of faith, offer the Agnihotra duly for three years—"

sanskrit: svadāriṇāṃ dharmadhure mahātmanāṃ; yathocite vartmani susthitānām dharmātmanām udvahatāṃ gatiṃ tāṃ; paraṃ gantā dhṛtarāṣṭro na tatra
english: "—who are content with their own wives, great-souled, who bear up the yoke of duty, standing firm upon the fitting path, righteous of soul—to their estate Dhṛtarāṣṭra, journeying onward, will not go."

sanskrit: gautama uvāca indrasya lokā virajā viśokā; duranvayāḥ kāṅkṣitā mānavānām tasyāhaṃ te bhavane bhūritejaso; rājann imaṃ hastinaṃ yātayiṣye
english: Gautama said: "The worlds of Indra, free of dust, free of sorrow, hard to reach yet longed for by men—in the dwelling of that one of abundant splendor, O king, will I haul you over this elephant."

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca śatavarṣajīvī yaś ca śūro manuṣyo; vedādhyāyī yaś ca yajvāpramattaḥ ete sarve śakralokaṃ vrajanti; paraṃ gantā dhṛtarāṣṭro na tatra
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: "The man who lives a hundred years and is a hero, he who studies the Veda, and the sacrificer who is ever vigilant—all these go to the world of Śakra; but Dhṛtarāṣṭra, journeying onward, will not go there."

sanskrit: gautama uvāca prājāpatyāḥ santi lokā mahānto; nākasya pṛṣṭhe puṣkalā vītaśokāḥ manīṣitāḥ sarvalokodbhavānāṃ; tatra tvāhaṃ hastinaṃ yātayiṣye
english: Gautama said: "There are the great worlds of Prajāpati, upon the vault of heaven, abundant, free of sorrow, longed for by those born into all the worlds—there will I haul you over this elephant."

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca ye rājāno rājasūyābhiṣiktā; dharmātmāno rakṣitāraḥ prajānām ye cāśvamedhāvabhṛthāplutāṅgās; teṣāṃ lokā dhṛtarāṣṭro na tatra
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: "Those kings consecrated by the Rājasūya, righteous of soul, protectors of their people, and those whose limbs have been bathed in the concluding ablution of the Aśvamedha—theirs are those worlds; but Dhṛtarāṣṭra will not go there."

sanskrit: gautama uvāca tataḥ paraṃ bhānti lokāḥ sanātanāḥ; supuṇyagandhā virajā vītaśokāḥ tasminn ahaṃ durlabhe tvāpradhṛṣye; gavāṃ loke hastinaṃ yātayiṣye
english: Gautama said: "Beyond that shine the eternal worlds, fragrant with holiness, free of dust, free of sorrow; in that world of cows, hard to win and unassailable, will I haul you over this elephant."

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca yo gosahasrī śatadaḥ samāṃ samāṃ; yo gośatī daśa dadyāc ca śaktyā tathā daśabhyo yaś ca dadyād ihaikāṃ; pañcabhyo vā dānaśīlas tathaikām
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: "He who, owning a thousand cows, gives away a hundred year after year; he who, owning a hundred, gives ten according to his power; he who has but ten and gives one here, or he of generous nature who has five and gives one—"

sanskrit: ye jīryante brahmacaryeṇa viprā; brāhmīṃ vācaṃ parirakṣanti caiva manasvinas tīrthayātrāparāyaṇās; te tatra modanti gavāṃ vimāne
english: "—and those Brahmins who grow old in chastity and ever preserve the sacred speech of Brahman, thoughtful men devoted to pilgrimage to the holy fords—they rejoice there in the celestial car of the cows."

sanskrit: prabhāsaṃ mānasaṃ puṇyaṃ puṣkarāṇi mahat saraḥ puṇyaṃ ca naimiṣaṃ tīrthaṃ bāhudāṃ karatoyinīm
english: Prabhāsa, the holy Mānasa, the Puṣkara lakes, the great lake, the holy ford of Naimiṣa, the Bāhudā, the Karatoyā,

sanskrit: gayāṃ gayaśiraś caiva vipāśāṃ sthūlavālukām tūṣṇīṃgaṅgāṃ daśagaṅgāṃ mahāhradam athāpi ca
english: Gayā and Gayaśiras, the Vipāśā, the Sthūlavālukā, the Tūṣṇīṃgaṅgā, the Daśagaṅgā, and likewise the Mahāhrada,

sanskrit: gautamīṃ kauśikīṃ pākāṃ mahātmāno dhṛtavratāḥ sarasvatīdṛṣadvatyau yamunāṃ ye prayānti ca
english: the Gautamī, the Kauśikī, the Pākā—those great-souled men of firm vows who go to the Sarasvatī, the Dṛṣadvatī, and the Yamunā—

sanskrit: tatra te divyasaṃsthānā divyamālyadharāḥ śivāḥ prayānti puṇyagandhāḍhyā dhṛtarāṣṭro na tatra vai
english: there they go, dwelling in celestial form, wearing celestial garlands, blessed, rich in holy fragrance; but Dhṛtarāṣṭra surely will not go there.

sanskrit: gautama uvāca yatra śītabhayaṃ nāsti na coṣṇabhayam aṇv api na kṣutpipāse na glānir na duḥkhaṃ na sukhaṃ tathā
english: Gautama said: "Where there is no fear of cold nor even the least fear of heat, no hunger or thirst, no weariness, neither pain nor likewise pleasure;"

sanskrit: na dveṣyo na priyaḥ kaś cin na bandhur na ripus tathā na jarāmaraṇe vāpi na puṇyaṃ na ca pātakam
english: "where there is none hateful and none dear, no kinsman and no foe, where there is neither old age nor death, neither merit nor sin—"

sanskrit: tasmin virajasi sphīte prajñāsattvavyavasthite svayaṃbhubhavane puṇye hastinaṃ me yatiṣyati
english: "—in that dustless, ample realm, established in wisdom and pure being, the holy dwelling of the Self-Existent One, shall my cause concerning the elephant be tried."

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca nirmuktāḥ sarvasaṅgebhyo kṛtātmāno yatavratāḥ adhyātmayogasaṃsthāne yuktāḥ svargagatiṃ gatāḥ
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: "Those freed from all attachments, perfected in soul, restrained in their vows, steadfast in the discipline of the inner Self, have attained the path to heaven."

sanskrit: te brahmabhavanaṃ puṇyaṃ prāpnuvantīha sāttvikāḥ na tatra dhṛtarāṣṭras te śakyo draṣṭuṃ mahāmune
english: "Those endowed with goodness here attain the holy dwelling of Brahman; there your Dhṛtarāṣṭra cannot be seen, great sage."

sanskrit: gautama uvāca rathantaraṃ yatra bṛhac ca gīyate; yatra vedī puṇḍarīkaiḥ stṛṇoti yatropayāti haribhiḥ somapīthī; tatra tvāhaṃ hastinaṃ yātayiṣye
english: Gautama said: "Where the Rathantara and the Bṛhat hymns are sung, where the altar is strewn with white lotuses, where the drinker of Soma comes drawn by his bay steeds—there will I haul you over this elephant."
